To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1-min slices of NVB are predictive of a range of other measured variables, and that the predictive power of NVB slices can be enhanced by coding multiple slices.

(a) 1-min slices have lower predictive validity than full-length slices; (b) predictive validity of cumulative slices is close to that of full-length slices; and (c) effect sizes of predictive validity of NVB are small.
1-min slices of NVBs have lower predictive validity than 2-min slices, and that predictive validity of slices increases when slices 1 and 3 are combined.

The main takeaway from our work is that
thin-slice coding of nonverbal communication can be a viable and useful alternative for some research questions.
thin-slice coding can be a viable option when coding time is limited, but researchers should be aware that predictive validity is lower than when coding is based upon full-length video.
